players.product: Xiyun C500/C600 training-inference GPGPU boards and modules (plus Xisi N inference GPUs), GPU servers and supernode/cluster solutions with the MXMACA software stack

quarterly_data.signal: 2025 annual report: operating revenue RMB 1,644,085,465.86, up 121.26% from RMB 743,071,582.31, which the company attributes to significantly higher GPU shipments as customers recognised and kept buying its products; gross margin 56.51% (+3.02 percentage points); net loss attributable to shareholders RMB -789,446,296.82 (loss narrowed 43.97%), net loss excluding non-recurring items RMB -829,700,534.04 (narrowed 20.52%); operating cash flow RMB -1,260,071,793.82. Quarterly revenue: Q1 RMB 320,415,255.58, Q2 RMB 594,515,728.77, Q3 RMB 321,154,567.57, Q4 RMB 407,999,913.94; Q4 net loss RMB -443,944,179.87.

2025 sales volume: training-inference GPU boards 33,649 units (+147.31%) and AI inference GPU boards 4,946 units (+866.02%); cumulative GPU sales passed 55,000 chips by end-2025, deployed in 10+ AI computing clusters. GPU products and accessories revenue RMB 1,630,746,470.51 (+132.74%, gross margin 56.17%); direct sales RMB 767,693,832.33 (+65.34%), distribution RMB 876,391,633.53 (+215.72%); domestic sales 99.85% of revenue. Materials were 81.72% of cost; packaging and test fees RMB 4,429.71 ten-thousand (+193.51%).
quarterly_data.figure: 33,649 training-inference boards (+147.31%); 4,946 inference boards (+866.02%); 55,000+ GPUs cumulative

quarterly_data.signal: Top five customers took RMB 101,045.60 ten-thousand, 61.46% of 2025 sales, with no related-party sales; names not disclosed. The five largest receivable balances (21.37%, 17.63%, 16.52%, 16.18% and 11.98%) were 83.69% of receivables at end-2025.
quarterly_data.figure: top five customers 61.46% of sales; related party 0%

quarterly_data.signal: Top five suppliers supplied RMB 145,028.40 ten-thousand, 82.34% of 2025 purchases, with no related-party purchases; names not disclosed. The five largest prepayments were 96.94% of prepayments (largest 46.99%, second 38.89%).

Supply chain (2025 annual report): MetaX says US government policy currently restricts its access to advanced-node wafer foundry and HBM supply; it works with some overseas foundry and packaging suppliers, and its HBM, EDA tools and some interface IP come mainly from overseas suppliers, some scarce and hard to replace domestically in the short term. To secure supply it ordered ahead from wafer and HBM suppliers and prepaid a high share of the price (prepayments RMB 83,427.99 ten-thousand at end-2025) and built strategic stock (inventory RMB 149,609.34 ten-thousand). It says it has made breakthroughs in localising wafer manufacturing, packaging and test, memory chips, EDA and IP, and achieved an all-domestic process in 2025.
quarterly_data.figure: prepayments RMB 83,427.99 ten-thousand; inventory RMB 149,609.34 ten-thousand

quarterly_data.signal: Products: MetaX launched the Xiyun C600, its first GPU on an all-domestic process, at WAIC on July 24, 2025, with more compute than the C500 and new precision and HBM technology; it reached risk production at the end of 2025. Its second-generation Xiyun GPUs use HBM3/HBM3e memory. Each GPU chip integrates 7 MetaXLink interfaces, which the company says gives interconnect bandwidth comparable to NVIDIA's H200, supporting 2-128 card topologies and supernodes; on a thousand-card cluster, full pre-training of a 128B MoE model ran at about 95% linearity with more than 14 days without failure. It has MCM and 2.5D CoWoS-S packaging design capability and is extending to 2.5D CoWoS-L and silicon-bridge packaging. The MXMACA software stack is compatible with 6,000+ CUDA applications and 1,000+ models and had more than 30 ten-thousand registered users by March 13, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 7 MetaXLink interfaces per chip; C600 risk production end-2025

quarterly_data.signal: R&D investment RMB 1,027,392,905.89 in 2025 (+14.04%), 62.49% of revenue, none capitalised; 675 R&D staff (73% of employees). Projects: a second-generation high-performance general-purpose GPU on a domestic supply chain (total budget RMB 136,977.30 ten-thousand; trial-production stage), a third-generation GPU on an advanced process (budget RMB 204,015.07 ten-thousand; R&D stage) and a first graphics-rendering GPU (budget RMB 110,000 ten-thousand; R&D stage). IPO-funded projects: new high-performance general-purpose GPU R&D and industrialisation (target December 2027), a next-generation AI inference GPU (December 2028) and high-performance GPU technology for frontier applications (December 2029).

Company outlook (2025 annual report): it expects revenue growth to stay high; with cost optimisation and expense control, gross margin and expense ratios should stabilise and new-product ramps keep contributing, so losses are expected to keep narrowing toward a turnaround (it cautions that revenue may not grow as expected and losses may persist for a period). 2026 plan: build on the Xiyun C500 and C600 as main products, launch more product lines for inference and scientific computing at an appropriate time, and advance R&D and industrialisation of next-generation products Xisuo X206 and Xiyun C700; keep deepening the domestic supply chain after achieving an all-domestic process in 2025.
